title: Floor-Based Arrangement Puzzles
tagline: Year 3 — One person per floor: ordering clues, gaps, adjacency and negative constraints

introduction.overview: A floor puzzle places people on the floors of a building, one per floor. It is a vertical row, so the same methods apply: pin down the extremes (top and bottom floors), join neighbours into chains, convert "exactly k floors between" into a floor-number gap of k + 1, and use "not on" clues last. The numbers on the floors make counting questions easy once the order is fixed.
introduction.placementRelevance: Floor and building puzzles are a standard set type in logical-reasoning rounds, usually with seven or eight people.
introduction.realWorldContext: Allocating offices, flats or storage levels under adjacency rules works the same way.

learningObjectives: Turn gap clues into floor-number differences
Use top and bottom floors as anchors

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Floor 1 is the lowest. "Immediately above" means floor number + 1. "Exactly k floors between" means a floor-number gap of k + 1.

coreDefinitions: Top floor: floor 7 in a seven-storey building. Ground or lowest floor: floor 1.
Immediately above X: the floor numbered one more than X's.
Gap clue: exactly k floors between X and Y means |floor(X) − floor(Y)| = k + 1.
Adjacent floors: floor numbers that differ by exactly 1.
Negative clue: says a floor is not X's; use it to eliminate options.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: A building is a column of numbered boxes. Each clue is a rule about the numbers of two people, so treat it as arithmetic on floor numbers.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Write floor numbers 1 to 7 down the page. Fix extremes, place chains, convert gap clues to differences of k + 1, and finish with the remaining free floors.

mainNarrative: Seven people live on floors 1 to 7. Charan lives on the top floor; Farhan lives immediately below Charan; Esha lives on floor 4; Amit lives immediately below Esha; exactly three floors lie between Bina and Divya; Gita lives lower than Amit; Bina does not live on floor 1. Start with the fixed ones: Charan 7, Farhan 6, Esha 4, Amit 3. The free floors are 1, 2 and 5.

Exactly three floors between Bina and Divya means their floor numbers differ by 4. Among the free floors 1, 2, 5 the only pair with a difference of 4 is 1 and 5. Bina does not live on floor 1, so Bina lives on floor 5 and Divya on floor 1.

Gita takes the last free floor, 2. Check the remaining clue: Gita (floor 2) lives lower than Amit (floor 3). The final order from floor 1 to 7 is Divya, Gita, Amit, Esha, Bina, Farhan, Charan. Always verify the final order against every clue.
Counting questions are now simple. People above Esha = 7 − 4 = 3, and the floors between Gita and Esha are 4 − 2 − 1 = 1.
For swap questions, write the order again, swap the two names and read the neighbour you are asked about.

deepDiveAspects.title: Contradiction check
deepDiveAspects.content: If a clue seems to fail, you have misplaced someone or misread a clue. Never force a clue to fit.

deepDiveAspects.title: Parity tricks
deepDiveAspects.content: A gap of 3 floors (difference 4) leaves only a few pairs, so such clues are strong anchors.

solvedExamples.title: Gap to difference
solvedExamples.question: Exactly 3 floors lie between the floors of Bina and Divya. What is the difference of their floor numbers?

steps.title: Between
steps.explanation: Three floors between means the numbers are 4 apart.

solvedExamples.whyItWorks: Floors 1 and 5, or 2 and 6, or 3 and 7.

solvedExamples.title: Chain
solvedExamples.question: Charan lives on the top floor of a 7-floor building. Farhan lives immediately below Charan and Esha lives on floor 4. On which floor does Farhan live?
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: Esha's floor does not affect Farhan.

solvedExamples.title: Counting above
solvedExamples.question: If Esha lives on floor 4 of a 7-floor building, how many people live above her?

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Write floor numbers, place extremes and chains, turn gaps into differences of k + 1, and use negatives last.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Cross out floors as you use them.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Use difference clues on the free floors only.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Unique puzzles never need a guess.
